REMARKS
Status of the Claims
This amendment is filed in response to the Office Action mailed September 5, 2024.
Claims 1 through 20 are pending in the application.
Claims 1 through 20 stand rejected.
Claims 1, 9, and 17-20 are amended herein.
Support for the amendments to independent claims 1, 9, and 17 can be found at least at pages 2, 5, and 14 (paragraphs [0004], [0014], and [0049] of the publication) and FIGS. 6B-6C of the as-filed application.
No new matter is added.
For at least the reasons presented below, Applicant respectfully submits that each of the pending claims is in condition for allowance.
Specification
The disclosure is objected to for informalities. Applicant has amended Equation 2 on page 10 of the specification to replace the term “Microscopically” with the term “Macroscopically.”
Thus, Applicant requests that the objections to the disclosure be withdrawn.
35 U.S.C. 112
Claims 1, 2, 5-11 and 14-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) as lacking enablement.
In an effort to further the prosecution of the present application, and not as an acquiescence to the rejections, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 9, and 17 herein.
Applicant asserts that the present claims, as currently amended, meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112, and thus, appear to be in condition for allowance.
35 U.S.C. 101
Claims 9-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 as allegedly directed to a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea) without significantly more.
In an effort to further the prosecution of the present application, and not as an acquiescence to the rejections, Applicant has amended independent claims 9 and 17 herein.
Applicant asserts that the present claims, as currently amended, meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, and thus, appear to be in condition for allowance.
35 U.S.C. 103
Claims 1-4, 9-13, and 17-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Kim et al. (Motion Artifact Reduction in Photoplethysmography Using Independent Component Analysis, IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng., VOL.53, NO.3, pp.566-568 (2006.03)) (hereinafter “Kim”) in view of Lee (The Motion Artifact Reduction from the PPG based on EWMA. Journal of Digital Convergence. 11, p. 183-190. August 2013) (hereinafter “Lee”).
To establish a prima facie case of obviousness, the prior art reference itself (or references when combined) or “the inferences and creative steps that a person of ordinary skill in the art would [have] employ[ed]” at the time of the invention must teach or suggest all of the claim elements. K.S.R. Intern. Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 418, 82 U.S.P.Q.2d 1385 (2007); see also M.P.E.P. § 2143.03. Additionally, the Examiner must determine whether there is “an apparent reason to combine the known elements in the fashion claimed by the patent at issue.” Id. “[A] patent composed of several elements is not proved obvious merely by demonstrating that each of its elements was, independently, known in the prior art.” Id. Further, rejections on obviousness grounds “cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness.” Id. (quoting In re Kahn, 441, F.3d 977, 988 (Fed. Cir. 2006)). Finally, to establish a prima facie case of obviousness there must be a reasonable expectation of success. In re Merck & Co., Inc., 800 F.2d 1091, 1097 (Fed. Cir. 1986). Furthermore, the reason that would have prompted the combination and the reasonable expectation of success must be found in the prior art, common knowledge, or the nature of the problem itself, and not based on the Applicant’s disclosure. DyStar Textilfarben GmbH & Co. Deutschland KG v. C. H. Patrick Co., 464 F.3d 1356, 1367 (Fed. Cir. 2006); MPEP § 2144. Underlying the obvious determination is the fact that hindsight cannot be used. KSR, 550 U.S. at 421; DyStar, 464 F.3dat 1367.
Applicant respectfully asserts that claims 1-4, 9-13, and 17-20 could not have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made considering Kim in view of Lee at least because Kim and Lee, when combined, do not teach or suggest each and every element recited in independent claim 1, 9, or 17, as currently amended. For example, Kim and Lee, when combined, do not teach or suggest restoring “the final PPG AC signal from the primarily restored PPG AC signal and a previous PPG signal not having distortion through block interleaving, and wherein the block interleaving utilizes an average of the last two or more primarily restored PPG AC signals to provide the restored final PPG AC signal,” as recited in each of claims 1, 9, and 17.
Kim teaches motion artifact reduction in PPG using independent component analysis. Kim, page 566, title. Kim further teaches that a preprocessor consists of period detection, block interleaving, low-pass filtering, and block de-interleaving. Id., page 567, section II. B. second paragraph. Kim does not appear to teach or suggest, however, restoring “the final PPG AC signal from the primarily restored PPG AC signal and a previous PPG signal not having distortion through block interleaving, and wherein the block interleaving utilizes an average of the last two or more primarily restored PPG AC signals to provide the restored final PPG AC signal,” as recited in each of claims 1, 9, and 17.
Lee teaches motion artifact reduction from a PPG utilizing an exponentially weighted moving average filter method. Lee, page 183, title and abstract. Lee does not appear to teach or suggest, however, restoring “the final PPG AC signal from the primarily restored PPG AC signal and a previous PPG signal not having distortion through block interleaving, and wherein the block interleaving utilizes an average of the last two or more primarily restored PPG AC signals to provide the restored final PPG AC signal,” as recited in each of claims 1, 9, and 17.
Rather than extracting the variation in PPG DC using EWMA filtering, based on the observation that the distortion levels of PPG AC and PPG DC are similar, and then back-calculating the distortion variation in PPG AC, Lee appears to employ EWMA merely to smooth localized distortions in PPG AC by utilizing the similarity of PPG cycles and previous PPG data. Thus, it appears that Lee and the present application share a similarity only in the use of EWMA filtering, but the EWMA filter is applied entirely differently.
Additionally, from the perspective of effectiveness, it appears that Lee cannot restore signals when significant distortions caused by PPG DC are observed by the sensor, as it appears limited to localized distortions in PPG AC. In contrast, the present invention enables real-time restoration even under such severe distortions.
Thus, independent claims 1, 9, and 17, and claims 2-4, 10-13, and 18-20 that depend therefrom, appear to be in condition for allowance.
Claims 5-7, 14 and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Kim in view of Lee (as stated above), further in view of Krishnan et al. ("Two-Stage Approach for Detection and Reduction of Motion Artifacts in Photoplethysmographic Data," in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, vol. 57, no. 8, pp. 1867-1876, Aug. 2010, doi: 10.1109/TBME.2009.2039568.) (hereinafter “Krishnan”).
As previously discussed herein, Kim and Lee do not teach or suggest each and every element recited in independent claim 1 or 9, as currently amended. Krishnan fails to cure the deficiencies of Kim and Lee with regard to claims 1 and 9. For example, Krishnan does not appear to teach or suggest restoring “the final PPG AC signal from the primarily restored PPG AC signal and a previous PPG signal not having distortion through block interleaving, and wherein the block interleaving utilizes an average of the last two or more primarily restored PPG AC signals to provide the restored final PPG AC signal,” as recited in each of claims 1 and 9.
Additionally, it appears that Krishnan uses PPG AC data regarding PPG AC distortion, rather than restoring PPG signals by utilizing PPG DC data, which has not been conventionally used.
Thus, independent claims 1 and 9, and claims 5-7, 14 and 15 that depend therefrom, appear to be in condition for allowance.
Claims 8 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Kim in view of Lee (as stated above), further in view of Wikipedia ("Field-programmable gate array." Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia. Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia, 2 Aug. 2021) (hereinafter “WikiFPGA”).
As previously discussed herein, Kim and Lee do not teach or suggest each and every element recited in independent claim 1 or 9, as currently amended. WikiFPGA fails to cure the deficiencies of Kim and Lee with regard to claims 1 and 9. For example, WikiFPGA does not appear to teach or suggest restoring “the final PPG AC signal from the primarily restored PPG AC signal and a previous PPG signal not having distortion through block interleaving, and wherein the block interleaving utilizes an average of the last two or more primarily restored PPG AC signals to provide the restored final PPG AC signal,” as recited in each of claims 1 and 9.
Thus, independent claims 1 and 9, and claims 8 and 16 that depend therefrom, appear to be in condition for allowance.
Conclusion
In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
If the Examiner believes a telephone conference would expedite prosecution of this application, please contact the undersigned at (801) 870-4092.
Respectfully submitted,
